A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same extreme video-token reduction work despite the changed title and terminology. All pages, equations, tables, figures, and references are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original video question-answering results, token-reduction comparisons, efficiency measurements, component ablations, and clustering visualizations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds an evaluated DyCoke comparison and accuracy-per-token results.

M1.justification: Clustering, token centroids, the spatial-temporal index map, and motion integration match across the Token Dynamics/VQToken renaming. However, v1 Equation 5 specifies nested attention operations, whereas v4 Equation 7 specifies codebook queries/keys and map-derived values in one attention operation. v4 Figure 1 still depicts two attention blocks, leaving an actual procedural change versus inconsistent reformulation unresolved.

E1.justification: v1 lists MLVU among six selected evaluation benchmarks. v4 omits MLVU but still claims six benchmarks while naming five. Neither supplies MLVU results, so actual removal of evaluation coverage cannot be distinguished from a documentation omission. The training corpus and five benchmarks with reported results remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v4 Table 3 adds DyCoke to the adaptive-length comparison in v1 Table 4. Comparator membership in the fixed-length, general efficiency, cross-benchmark, and video-language-model comparisons otherwise remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 adds TokDense, accuracy divided by retained token count, to the evaluation metrics. Training budgets, model size, fixed token budgets, and existing compression settings remain unchanged. Throughput is relabeled clips/second in Section 4.4, although Section 4.1.4 says frames/second; this reporting inconsistency does not establish changed measurements.

E4.justification: Table 6 extends the component ablation with per-configuration TokDense values, adding an accuracy-per-token analysis. Component combinations, parameter-randomization tests, and their existing outcomes are retained. The K-Means-versus-SAM visualization and MVBench subtask analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Randomized component ablations occur in both and do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v4 adds DyCoke results of 57.70 accuracy with 1662.12 average tokens, plus TokDense entries. Table 1 changes the adaptive token count from 16 to 13.08, already reported in v1 Table 4. Other matched scores are unchanged apart from rounding. The headline loss changes from 1.13% to 0.66%, but the underlying 58.38 and 57.72 accuracies remain unchanged: these correspond to relative-percent and percentage-point differences.

T1.justification: v4 introduces the formal TokDense definition in Equation 2 and explicitly defines codebook entries as unweighted cluster means, replacing v1's reference to a general weighted merging formula. No new theorems, proofs, or substantive complexity derivations are supplied.

C1.justification: The central contribution is redefined from disentangled visual/motion Token Dynamics to a neural discrete-token framework claimed to be the first use of vector quantization for video-LLM token reduction. TokDense becomes a headline contribution. The extreme-compression and competitive cross-benchmark claims otherwise persist.

C2.justification: v4 adds a substantive explanation that continuous, neighboring tokens retain redundancy and low information density, motivating discrete codebook representations. Results are consequently interpreted in terms of information density as well as motion preservation. The existing component-necessity and K-Means/SAM efficiency interpretations remain, without new substantive failure conditions.

D1.justification: v4 adds a promise to release code and pretrained models upon acceptance. It omits v1 Section 3.5's explicit disclosure of using the original projection layer and end-to-end training with the original vLLM loss. Hardware, optimizer, learning rates, iterations, batch size, and gradient accumulation remain documented with the same values.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts toward claimed priority in vector-quantized token reduction and explicitly identifies prior methods' lack of discrete representations as a central gap. v4 also adds AuroraCap, VideoOrion, and DyCoke references and removes the MLVU reference. The magnitude comes principally from the revised novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method exposition, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around VQToken terminology. The standalone ToMe preliminaries and integration section disappear, method subsections are consolidated, and experimental setup sections are reorganized. The author block also changes.

P2.justification: v4 changes the document from two columns to one, redraws the framework diagram, and substantially rearranges tables and figures. Fixed/adaptive tables are placed side by side; clustering and MVBench figures are colocated and exchange numbering. TokDense columns and the DyCoke row alter table structures, while the underlying clustering images and MVBench plot are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens the adaptive comparison with DyCoke and adds an explicit accuracy-per-token measure. However, its revised attention equation conflicts with the retained two-block diagram, and explicit integration/loss information from v1 disappears. With most empirical findings unchanged, these gains in comparative evidence and losses in methodological clarity leave the overall quality direction uncertain.
